what_its_for: Bimekizumab-Bkzx is used to treat moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in adults whose psoriasis covers a large area of the body or is hard to treat with other medicines. It works by blocking certain proteins in your immune system (called IL-17A and IL-17F) that cause the redness, scaling, and inflammation seen in psoriasis.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as an injection just under the skin (subcutaneous injection). It comes in a prefilled syringe or autoinjector pen. Your doctor or nurse will train you on how to give yourself the shot at home. Common injection spots include your stomach (abdomen), thighs, or upper arms. Rotate injection sites each time and avoid skin that is red, bruised, tender, or affected by psoriasis. Let the pen or syringe warm up at room temperature for about 30 minutes before injecting. Do not shake the device.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 320 mg (given as two separate 160 mg injections at the same visit) every 4 weeks for the first 5 doses (weeks 0, 4, 8, 12, and 16). After that, the maintenance dose is 320 mg every 8 weeks. Always follow the exact dosing schedule your doctor gives you.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, give yourself the injection as soon as you remember. Then reschedule your next dose based on that new date, keeping at least the proper number of weeks between doses. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Call your doctor or pharmacist if you are not sure what to do.
storage: Store Bimzelx in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C). Keep it in the original carton to protect it from light. Do not freeze it and do not use it if it has been frozen. If needed, you may store it at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 5 days, but then it must be used or thrown away. Do not put it back in the refrigerator after it has been kept at room temperature. Keep it out of reach of children. Dispose of used syringes and pens in an FDA-approved sharps disposal container.
what_to_avoid: Avoid receiving live vaccines (such as the shingles vaccine Zostavax, live flu nasal spray, or yellow fever vaccine) while using this medicine, as it may make them less safe or effective. Tell all of your doctors and your pharmacist that you are taking this medicine before getting any vaccine. Avoid close contact with people who have active infections. Do not start this medicine if you have an active infection, including active tuberculosis (TB).
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: signs of a serious infection such as fever, chills, muscle aches, cough, shortness of breath, or skin that is warm, red, and painful; symptoms of inflammatory bowel disease such as new or worsening stomach pain, cramping, or diarrhea; signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, difficulty breathing, or dizziness; or any new or unusual symptoms that worry you. Also let your doctor know before starting this medicine if you have a history of TB, Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, or any recurring infections.
when_it_works: Some people start to see improvement in their skin within 4 weeks of starting treatment. Many patients see significant clearing by week 16. Results can vary from person to person, so keep taking your medication as scheduled even if you do not notice changes right away. Talk to your doctor if you feel the medicine is not working after a few months.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: It is not known whether this medicine can harm an unborn baby or pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before using this medicine. Children: Bimzelx has not been studied in children and is not approved for use in anyone under 18 years of age. Older adults: No dose adjustment is needed based on age alone, but older adults may be at higher risk for infections, so follow up with your doctor regularly. Inflammatory bowel disease: Use caution if you have a history of Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, as this medicine may worsen these conditions.
